name: ticketer.py - Forge ExtraSids Golden Ticket (Child→Parent)
description: Forges a golden ticket with the ExtraSids extension — includes the parent domain's Enterprise Admins SID in the ticket's SID history. This makes the forged child-domain ticket be treated as Enterprise Admin in the parent domain. Enables full parent domain compromise from a child domain KRBTGT hash alone.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== THE EXTRASIDS ATTACK (CHILD → PARENT) ===
When you compromise a child domain (LOGISTICS.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL), you can
escalate to the parent domain (INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL) without any credentials there.

How: Kerberos SID history allows tickets to include SIDs from previous migrations.
By adding the parent domain's Enterprise Admins SID (RID 519) to the SID history
of a forged child domain golden ticket, the parent DC sees Enterprise Admin rights.

=== WHAT YOU NEED ===
  1. Child domain KRBTGT NT hash (from secretsdump of child DC)
  2. Child domain SID (lookupsid.py or Get-DomainSID)
  3. Parent domain Enterprise Admins SID:
     → lookupsid.py against parent DC → find RID 519
     → S-1-5-21-[PARENT-DOMAIN-SID]-519
  4. Any username to put in the ticket (Administrator is traditional)

=== ARGUMENTS ===
  -nthash         → child KRBTGT NT hash
  -domain         → child domain FQDN
  -domain-sid     → child domain SID (S-1-5-21-...)
  -extra-sid      → parent's Enterprise Admins SID (S-1-5-21-[parent]-519)
  Administrator   → username to put in the ticket (doesn't need to exist!)

Output: Administrator.ccache

=== USING THE TICKET ===
export KRB5CCNAME=Administrator.ccache
psexec.py LOGISTICS.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL/Administrator@ACADEMY-EA-DC01.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL \
  -k -no-pass -target-ip 172.16.5.5

=== AUTOMATED ALTERNATIVE ===
raiseChild.py -target-exec <parent_dc_ip> <child_domain>/<child_admin>:<pass>
Does all of the above automatically: dumps child KRBTGT, builds ExtraSids ticket,
executes on parent DC.

=== MIMIKATZ EQUIVALENT ===
kerberos::golden /user:Administrator /domain:LOGISTICS.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL
  /sid:S-1-5-21-[child] /krbtgt:<hash> /sids:S-1-5-21-[parent]-519 /ptt

=== WHY PARENT DOMAIN IS FULLY COMPROMISED ===
Enterprise Admins have full rights over ALL domains in the forest — including
adding accounts to Domain Admins everywhere, modifying all objects, and DCSync.

examples.label: Export ticket and psexec to parent DC

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

recommended.note: Use the forged ticket to get a SYSTEM shell on the parent DC.

defense.why_it_works: ticketer.py forges a Kerberos TGT for the child domain (signed with child KRBTGT hash) and inserts the parent domain's Enterprise Admins SID (S-1-5-21-[parent]-519) into the PAC's ExtraSids field (SID history). When this ticket is used across the parent-child trust, the parent's KDC processes the inter-realm referral and reads the ExtraSids field — because SID history is honoured in trust transitions by default, the parent grants Enterprise Admin privileges. The ticket is saved as a .ccache file and used via KRB5CCNAME.
defense.prerequisites: Child domain KRBTGT NT hash (from DCSync of child DC). Child domain SID. Parent domain's Enterprise Admins SID (S-1-5-21-[parent]-519 — obtained via lookupsid.py against parent DC). Linux host with Impacket. DNS or /etc/hosts entry for parent DC FQDN.
defense.impact: Forged ticket granting Enterprise Admin rights in the parent (root) domain — full forest compromise. From this ticket: psexec to parent DC → SYSTEM shell → DCSync the entire parent domain → golden ticket for parent persistence. All parent-domain resources and child domain resources are now accessible.
defense.detection: Kerberos cross-realm authentication events on the parent DC with anomalous PAC content (SID history field containing SIDs not belonging to the child domain). Event 4768/4769 on both child and parent DCs with cross-forest referral chain. Microsoft Defender for Identity detects ExtraSids attacks specifically — the PAC SID value (519) from a child-domain principal is anomalous. The .ccache file on the attacker's Linux disk is also an artifact.
defense.artifacts: Administrator.ccache ticket file on attacker's disk; KRB5CCNAME environment variable; Event 4768 (TGT request) on child DC; cross-realm Kerberos referral traffic; Event 4769 on parent DC with child-domain principal requesting parent resources; subsequent Event 4624 + 7045 on parent DC if psexec follows.
defense.prevention: Enable SID Filtering on the parent-child trust (neutralises ExtraSids by stripping non-domain SIDs from PAC). This is the most direct mitigation — note it may break some legitimate cross-domain resource access scenarios; test before deploying in production. Reset child domain KRBTGT to prevent DCSync data being leveraged. Deploy MDI across all forest domains. Treat child domain compromise as a forest-level incident requiring full investigation.
defense.evasion: Ticket exists only on the Linux attacker's filesystem as a .ccache — no Windows memory artifacts until used. KRB5CCNAME env var sets which ticket is used; rename the file to something less obvious. Operate quickly after forging — the ticket has a default 10-hour lifetime (set explicitly if needed to match policy). Combine with -aes256 key option for AES tickets if the AES key was extracted during DCSync.
defense.misconfiguration: Domain trusts (especially bidirectional and forest trusts) extend authentication boundaries. SID filtering is often disabled on forest trusts to support legacy applications — but this allows an attacker with Domain Admin in a child domain to forge a golden ticket with ExtraSids claiming Domain Admin SID in the parent/trusted forest. Without SID filtering (SIDHistory filtering), domain boundaries offer no security isolation.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Bidirectional forest trust without SID filtering:
Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select-Object Name, Direction, SIDFilteringQuarantined
# SIDFilteringQuarantined: False  <-- SID filtering DISABLED
# Direction: BiDirectional        <-- both domains trust each other

# Child domain to parent: SID filtering is always disabled by default
# Enterprise Admin SID (S-1-5-21-<root>-519) can be added to ExtraSids
# Golden ticket with ExtraSids = cross-domain privilege escalation
defense.secure_config:
# Enable SID filtering on external/forest trusts:
netdom trust <TrustingDomain> /domain:<TrustedDomain> /quarantine:yes
# 'Quarantine' = SID filtering enabled — ExtraSids from other domain are stripped

# For child-to-parent trusts (SID filtering can't be enabled without breaking functionality):
# Use Selective Authentication instead of full trust
# Only accounts explicitly granted 'Allowed to Authenticate' can use the trust
netdom trust <ParentDomain> /domain:<ChildDomain> /SelectiveAuth:yes

# Restrict SIDHistory (prevents ExtraSids abuse):
# Audit accounts with SIDHistory:
Get-ADUser -Filter {SIDHistory -like '*'} -Properties SIDHistory

# Monitor cross-forest authentication:
# Event 4769 on parent DC with ticket from child domain user
